decisions.title: Visibility & access model (final)
decisions.note: Settled via the worked-example artifact. THREE plan access modes: OPEN (book immediately) · OPEN + REQUEST-ACCESS (visible to all, approval-required → request→approve→book) · EXCLUSIVE (offered to specific resellers; HIDDEN from everyone else — they never see it exists; NOT shown-but-locked, per Alejandro Herrero: see-but-can't-buy creates frustration). Per-reseller states: Bookable / Request access (🔒, only the open-to-all+approval case) / Hidden (🚫, an exclusive you're not on) / Removed (✕). Removal ops: BLOCK a distributor = cut them from ALL of one partner's events (unifies the former O-12 'revoke') + cancel pending reservations (confirmed kept, no new bookings); UNPUBLISH a plan for a reseller = pull one plan for one reseller (e.g. open→exclusive switch — confirmed kept, pending cancelled, open cart cleared); UNPUBLISH for everyone = pull from the marketplace (bookings stay payable). Card 'from' price = each group's lowest qualifying price, served either via a per-group materialized view OR a written 'from' field in FeverZone (materialization optional). Group = an exclusive offered to a SET of resellers — same hide mechanic, no separate model. Refines the 2026-06-23 pricing decision on the visibility dimension. — REFINED 2026-07-08: formalized as a relationship-state machine (Pending · Approved·Open-only · Approved·Full-catalog · Rejected); 'Hidden' is now expressed purely through group/channel publication, not a separate flag; per-distributor state is DERIVED from the relationship state + group publication. ⚠ UNDER REVISION 2026-07-09 — the catalog-request ↔ relationship governance is being reworked with design (mute/Ignored may be dropped for a terminal Rejected CTA).

decisions.title: Pricing structure: B2BM price-list inheritance + group model
decisions.note: ⚠️ REFINED 2026-06-26 by the 'Visibility & access model (final)' decision above — read together, not in isolation: point (2) 'catalog buyable by all distributors' holds only for OPEN events; EXCLUSIVE events are now HIDDEN from non-grantees (not shown-but-locked), and OPEN+REQUEST-ACCESS events are visible but approval-gated. So 'buyable by all' = the open catalog, not every event. — Original (validated 06-23): (1) A channel/group price list inherits from the B2B-marketplace price list, NEVER the generic base (retail-leak risk); the base is only the clone-source at creation. (2) The B2BM catalog is buyable by all distributors; group specificity = B2B discount per ticket + optional ticket-type-level visibility (aggregation, not inheritance). (3) MVP red-line: groups set only prices, no group-specific ticket types. Does NOT resolve the still-open 'auto-inherit global B2B discount?' or 'B2B discount min/max legal cap?' questions. — SUPERSEDED 2026-07-08 by the CLOSED price-list model: b2b-discount is a mandatory field on every price-list row (backfilled 0%); the winning list gives retail price + discount from the SAME row with NO fallback to a parent/base list (the earlier 'inherits from the B2B-marketplace list' mechanic is dropped); a group IS a sales channel. — CONFIRMED 2026-08-07 against fever2 `src/core/domain/price_list/`: PriceList.main_plan scopes a list to ONE event (never shared); applies_to_all_channels + the PriceListChannel join table do the channel restriction; PriceListItem.session_type makes the TICKET TYPE the pricing unit. Andrea re-confirmed a distributor group CREATES the Channel. ⚠ NOTE: PriceList.parent_price_list exists in the model, and a 2026-08-07 pass briefly wrote into SYS-01/O-04/O-16 that channel lists INHERIT through it — that was wrong and was corrected the same day. The 2026-07-08 closed model stands: single-row resolution, no parent fallback.

decisions.title: Wholesale reservation management at launch: customer info editable, cancel not available

(2) A DISTRIBUTOR CANNOT CANCEL — cancel was removed from D-07a, which is now view + edit customer info only. Pulling this scope into the MVP converted a 28-day-stalled design ticket into a Wholesales-launch blocker. ⚠ THREE EARLIER RECORDS ARE NOW VOID: the D-07 split rationale (justified by cancel landing in the launch); D-14's deletion reason ('no change to be done', read as cancel reusing the existing refund path — there is no distributor cancel to reuse one); and DEC-025 (wholesale cancellation policy, open and unowned) which is either resolved by this or concerns a different actor. ⚠ STILL OPEN: can anyone cancel at all — the organizer path is described in no story and unsized as launch support load; and whether 're-share Pay-by-Link' survives on its own, having been bundled into the removed cancel criterion. ⚠ The substantive engineering work is TICKET RE-ISSUANCE, not the form: tickets are issued on payment (D-06/D-06b) and the resale happens after, so changing the customer must decide whether the issued ticket is reissued, its previous delivery invalidated, or both left live. Unspecified. ⚠ PERSONAL DATA: the customer is a third party with no Fever relationship whose details a distributor types in; lawful basis, retention and controller appear nowhere in the plan, nor in B2BR-5522's acceptance criteria. ⚠ EFFORT: D-07a's 1 week and D-07b's 2 weeks were an assistant division of D-07's original 3 weeks, never squad-sized. D-07a has since gained paid-order customer editing and ticket re-issuance and lost cancel. Deliberately NOT re-estimated — the Oct 12 / Oct 26 dates are unchanged on paper but now carry an un-priced change and a live blocker.

fzImpact.title: FeverZone impact
fzImpact.summary: Deposits lives inside FeverZone's reservation/cart engine end-to-end — creation, cart preview/modification, payment, cancellation and refund all gained deposit-awareness. The riskiest surface is the current “single main plan, two carts” approach: a deposit payment is a special order that must be excluded or special-cased in every order-based flow (partner order list, inventory, notifications, finance-billing, access-control, reporting). A “Payment/order decoupling” redesign (dedicated PaymentGroup/PaymentCharge entities, no Order created until settlement) is fully specced in the tracker as the long-term fix but is not yet an active build. Finance-billing gained a full deposit/settlement/credit-note domain (b2c + b2b) on the same PayableEntryRecordedEvent pipeline B2BM's commission work also uses.

refactors.change: Cart/Deposit entity split (source_cart → Deposit PENDING/PAID → remaining-amount recalculation); three settlement paths (Path A one-shot / Path B skip-to-full / Path C deposit-aware remainder) added to the existing reservation-payment endpoints so they stay deposit-aware without double-charging.

New pass-through item builders (DepositItemBuilder, RemainderItemBuilder) route by b2c_order.intent (DEPOSIT/SETTLEMENT/REFUND) through the existing reconciler→assigner→resolver pipeline; b2b_transaction rows + per-leg commission computation for reconciliation invoices.

Under the current approach, every order-based flow (partner order list, inventory session-type exclusion, notifications, access-control, reporting) must exclude or special-case “deposit orders” — flagged in the tracker as the main tech-debt/double-count risk driver.

~18 partner-export DAGs (SAP/CAPN, LivGolf, RAPI deliver exports, TBAI, United Parks, UNICEF, Rauda, Superfly, Bandsintown, etc.) individually assessed for deposit-line impact in the tracker; most affected only if/when a given partner needs a deposit line in their export (Data team owns; doesn't block rollout).
